Major banks such as Bank of America [d1], Wells Fargo [d2], U.S. Bank [d6], Chase [d7], and Fifth Third Bank [d8] all offer home mortgage loans, allowing borrowers to compare rates, prequalify, and apply in person or online. Online lenders like Rocket Mortgage [d5] and credit unions like Navy Federal Credit Union [d9] also provide mortgage applications entirely online, with preapproval available through digital platforms. For eligible borrowers, government-backed programs through the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) are additional sources of home loans [d3]. You may also work with a mortgage broker, who acts as a third party between you and the lender, though this typically involves extra fees [d4].
